results.title: Live: France mobilises in fifth wave of student protests
results.content: Between 50 and 60 marches are expected in France on Saturday, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, who plans to mobilise approximately 70,000 police officers and gendarmes across the country. In Paris, the march will commence at 1pm from Place de la République heading towards Place de la Nation via Bastille.

results.title: Microsoft says all services 'fully recovered' after global outage
results.content: The tech giant confirmed on Saturday morning that all services have recovered ⁠across ‌Teams, Outlook, Copilot and ⁠other applications, ​ending a ‌global outage ‌that ​crippled online communications across businesses and ​governments ​for ​over 24 hours. The US homeland security chief confirmed there was 'no Microsoft link' to the US air stoppage.

results.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop on all US flights
results.content: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation's airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was not due to a cyberattack or a sweeping Microsoft outage.

results.title: US flights resume after nationwide ground stop lifted
results.content: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation's airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was not due to a cyberattack or a sweeping Microsoft outage. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that US airspace was now "opened up," and blamed "old hardware" for the travel chaos.

results.title: US flights resume gradually amid further cancellations
results.content: While flights in the United States started resuming on Saturday following the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years, more than 2,000 flights have been cancelled as airlines work to return to normal operations. Nearly 6,000 flights were cancelled on Friday, with the incident marking only the second time an alert to ground all flights had been issued in US airspace since the 9/11 attacks.

results.title: France secures thrilling Nations Championship victory over South Africa
results.content: France smashed world ⁠champions South ​Africa's hopes of lifting the first Nations Championship trophy on Friday, in a ​21-19 defeat for Les Bleus.

results.title: Gambia's Adama Barrow seeks third term
results.content: In tonight's programme, Gambia's electoral commission has announced the five official candidates for the country's upcoming presidential election. President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term. Tensions continue to rise in Ethiopia following the federal government's appointment of a new head of the Western Tigray region. And the Dakar Youth Olympic Games come to a close after two weeks of intense competition.

results.title: France among five major powers to represent EU in Ukraine talks
results.content: European Council President Antonio Costa on Friday said that Brussels will send diplomats from the bloc and five countries, including the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, to upcoming Ukraine talks.

results.title: 🔴 US flight authority orders national ground stop over air traffic control 'communication issue'
US flight authority orders national ground stop over air traffic control 'communication issue'
results.content: The US flight authority on Friday halted flights across the nation due to what US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said was a communication issue affecting the country's air traffic control centres.

results.title: Turkey and Qatar pledge unified stance against attacks in mutual defence pact
results.content: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, the two leaders said in a joint statement. The defence pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.

results.title: The Downfall of AI’s ‘Rock Star’ Boss, Ukraine: Who speaks for Europe? Protests & Presidents
results.content: On The World This Week with Gavin Lee, our panel distills the breaking news and global stories of the past 7 days into 45 minutes. Ukraine: Who will speak for Europe? In a week thats seen the first direct talks between Ukraine and Russia since February, with the US in the room and the Europeans relegated to the lobby according to Moscow. A new ‘European Security Architecture’ is discussed.

results.title: Hurry up and wait: Europe wants a place at the table, ‘must make up its mind’ over Ukraine
results.content: Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Alexander Titov, Lecturer in Modern European History at Queen's University Belfast and a specialist on Russia. He's joined us to discuss high-level meetings in Abu Dhabi, Dublin and the prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.

results.title: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
results.content: China has been carrying out major military drills around Taiwan since early November. But contrary to some claims on social media, Beijing's armed forces have not actually implemented a blockade on the island; they just simulated it.

results.title: 'We have done all our homework' to get EU candidate status: Kosovo's PM Albin Kurti
results.content: FRANCE 24 hosts Albin Kurti, the prime minister of Kosovo, a country that declared its independence from Serbia back in 2008 and sees itself as part of the European family. But four years after applying to join the EU, Kosovo has still not received candidate status. We explore Kosovo's path towards the EU, and the broader European and regional dynamics surrounding that.

results.title: As EU grapples with fierce AI competition, summit overshadowed by elusive Ukraine-Russia peace deal
results.content: As EU leaders meet for an AI summit in Dublin, largely overshadowed by Russia's war on Ukraine, William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome Fabrice Pothier, CEO of Rasmussen Global. On AI, Pothier points to Europe's limited computing capacity, estimating that it barely represents "5% of what's available out there." Despite the EU's wealth of researchers and expertise, he warns that Europe is struggling to turn these resources into "real technological and industrial scale." Now, turning to the war in Ukraine, Pothier argues that European governments should focus less on "whether they have a place at the table" and more on "making Ukraine's hands stronger," particularly by providing additional air defence interceptors.

results.title: The Nvidia affair: Are markets about to fall out of love with AI?
results.content: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia exposes the vulnerabilities behind the AI boom. As equities reel in response to his resignation following extramarital affairs, alleged Chinese espionage and a summons to testify before US lawmakers, questions mount over who is really in charge of tech and whether the immense capital riding on it can survive the turmoil.

results.title: November 13 Paris attacks: Eleven years later, France pays tribute to victims
results.content: Eleven years on, France pays tribute to the victims of the November 13 attacks. French officials, victims’ associations and families gathered this Friday to pay their respects to those killed in the attacks in Paris on November 13, 2015.

results.title: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'
results.content: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace. People taking it had to navigate extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. What has become of the road after the US-led war and five years of Taliban rule? Our former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to find out.

results.title: Myanmar: Junta carries out double-tap airstrikes targeting civilians
results.content: Numerous civilian casualties have been documented in Rakhine State amid a renewed military offensive by the junta to regain control of the area. Available evidence suggests that military aircraft are deliberately targeting civilian sites and carrying out double-tap strikes.

results.title: El Niño fuels climate disasters: The high price of inaction
results.content: 2026 is set to be one of the hottest years on record, with El Niño worsening the impact of extreme weather events. With COP31 underway in Turkey, FRANCE 24 speaks with the UNDP's climate boss about the cost of waiting in a warmer world, and with one of the student activists from Pacific Island nations who took their climate fight to the UN's highest court, and won.

results.title: West Bank: ‘Without international trade and financial support, large settlements would not exist’
results.content: France is considering legislation to restrict trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, namely the West Bank. Ivar Ekeland, Professor Emeritus at Paris Dauphine-PSL University and Chair of the Organization of Academics for the Respect of International Law in Palestine, discusses the proposed measures with Alison Sargent. He calls for restrictions to cover n ot only goods but also services, including financial services, insurance and tourism. "Without the support of financial entities, of insurance, of providing goods and so on, settlements, big settlements, would not exist," he argues.

results.title: UN refugee chief Barham Salih slams 'shameful' war in Sudan, urges 'political solution'
results.content: In an interview with FRANCE 24, UN refugee chief Barham Salih called the war in Sudan "shameful" and urged the world to end it. With forced displacement at a record high, he warned that funding cuts are hurting people "in dire need". "Efficiency has its limits," he said. Salih also defended the "integrity of the asylum system".

results.title: France asks Brussels to examine Algeria's non-compliance of EU association agreement
results.content: France announced on Friday that it will ask the European Commission to "examine" Algeria's non-compliance with its EU association agreement. Earlier in July, Algiers imposed a near-blanket ban on French imports, and last month, Algeria suspended urea shipments to France.
